person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We show that this coupling significantly slows the diffusion process, resulting in dynamic trapping of information in communities, and find that when it comes to information diffusion, weak and strong ties are both simultaneously ineffective.

span.label: tie strength and local topology in mobile communication networks
span.quote: Here we examine the communication patterns of millions of mobile phone users, allowing us to simultaneously study the local and the global structure of a society-wide communication network.

span.label: network-analysis
span.quote: A significant portion of a country’s communication network was reconstructed from 18 weeks of all mobile phone call records among approximately 20% of the country’s entire population, 90% of whose inhabitants had a mobile phone subscription (see Supporting Information).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: weak ties bridge otherwise-separate communities, so removing them fragments the network via a percolation-like phase transition (a societal-scale confirmation of Granovetter strength-of-weak-ties)
span.quote: This result is broadly consistent with the strength of weak ties hypothesis, offering its first societal-level confirmation

span.label: The reconstructed graph covers only mobile voice calls, not the full range of interactions between people.
span.note: what this limits: every claim about social ties from this graph: THE MCG CAPTURES ONLY A SUBSET OF ALL INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS, [excluding] FACE-TO-FACE, EMAIL AND LANDLINE
span.quote: Note that the MCG captures only a subset of all interactions between individuals, a detailed mapping of which would require face-to-face, email and landline communications as well.

span.label: The reciprocity requirement used to define a link may discard genuine social ties (false negatives).
span.note: what this limits: the link definition: the reciprocity requirement INDUCES SOME FALSE NEGATIVES, I.E. SOME LINKS CORRESPONDING TO GENUINE SOCIAL INTERACTION MAY GO UNDETECTED
span.quote: It is possible that this induces some false negatives, i.e. some links corresponding to genuine social interaction may go undetected.

span.label: The data are a single-operator sample of the underlying national call network, not the whole population network.
span.note: what this limits: any population-level reading: ALTHOUGH THE DATASET COVERS SOME SEVEN MILLION USERS, IT IS NEVERTHELESS A SAMPLE OF THE UNDERLYING PHONE CALL NETWORK - scale is not coverage
span.quote: Although the dataset covers some seven million users, it is nervertheless a sample of the underlying phone call network that consists of all mobile users in the country.

span.label: The strength of a social tie is measured as the total time two people spent on the phone.
span.note: what this limits: any claim here about the strength of social ties: strength is defined as the aggregated duration of calls between two users, after one-way calls have been eliminated by a reciprocity requirement
span.quote: as the aggregated duration of calls between users A and B. This procedure eliminates a large number of one-way calls, most of which correspond to single events, suggesting that they typically reach individuals that the caller does not know personally

span.label: The network studied is a stand-in for the communication network, and the paper says so.
span.note: what this limits: conclusions drawn here about human communication: the mobile call graph is used as a proxy for the communication network between users, being skewed toward trusted interactions because people share mobile numbers only with those they trust
span.quote: Therefore, the MCG can be used as a proxy of the communication network between the users

span.label: Three incompatible accounts of what drives tie strength were on the table before the measurement.
span.note: what this limits: the interpretation of the correlation reported here: the paper sets out a dyadic hypothesis, in which strength is independent of the surrounding network, against the strength of weak ties hypothesis, in which strength increases with friendship-circle overlap
span.quote: Another possiblility is that the strength of a particular tie depends only on the nature of the relationship between two individuals, and is thus independent of the network surrounding the tie (dyadic hypothesis). Finally, the much studied strength of weak ties hypothesis (18, 19, 20) states that the strength of a tie between A and B increases with the overlap of their friendship circles, resulting in the importance of weak ties in connecting communities

span.label: The conclusion sits between the positions rather than choosing one.
span.note: what this limits: the finding as support for any single theory of tie strength: the authors state it is in part driven by local network structure, in contrast with both a purely dyadic view and a global view
span.quote: It suggests that tie strength is, in part, driven by the network structure in the tie’s immediate vicinity. This is in contrast with a purely dyadic view, according to which the tie strength is determined only by the characteristics of the individuals it connects, or the global view, which asserts that tie strength is driven by the whole network topology

span.label: percolation and network analysis (robustness, phase transitions) applied to a society-scale communication network
span.quote: social networks are robust to the removal of the strong ties, but fall apart following a phase transition if the weak ties are removed

span.label: tie strength - AS AGGREGATED CALL DURATION: the sociological construct is measured by total air time between two people, over links that survive a reciprocity filter, so a strong tie here means many minutes and nothing else
span.quote: as the aggregated duration of calls between users A and B

span.label: what determines tie strength - THREE NAMED AND INCOMPATIBLE ANSWERS: a global efficiency principle in which strengths are optimised for overall flow, a dyadic hypothesis in which strength is independent of the surrounding network, and the strength of weak ties hypothesis in which it rises with friendship-circle overlap
span.quote: Complex networks often organize themselves according to a global efficiency principle, meaning that the tie strengths are optimized to maximize the overall flow in the network (13, 14). In this case the weight of a link should correlate with its betweenness centrality, which is proportional to the number of shortest paths between all pairs of nodes passing through it (13, 15, 16, 17). Another possiblility is that the strength of a particular tie depends only on the nature of the relationship between two individuals, and is thus independent of the network surrounding the tie (dyadic hypothesis). Finally, the much studied strength of weak ties hypothesis (18, 19, 20) states that the strength of a tie between A and B increases with the overlap of their friendship circles, resulting in the importance of weak ties in connecting communities

span.label: the mobile call graph - AS A PROXY, AND A SKEWED ONE BY DESIGN: it stands in for the communication network and is biased toward trusted interactions, because people share mobile numbers only with individuals they trust
span.quote: the mobile phone data is skewed towards trusted interactions (that is, people tend to share their mobile numbers only with individuals they trust). Therefore, the MCG can be used as a proxy of the communication network between the users

span.label: contradicts → the dyadic hypothesis and the global efficiency principle
span.quote: In this paper, taking advantage of society-wide data collection capabilities offered by mobile phone logs, we show that tie strengths correlate with the local network structure around the tie, and both the dyadic hypothesis and the global efficiency principle are unable to account for the empirical observations.

span.label: contradicts → the received account of weak ties as the conduits of novel information (Granovetter; Csermely)
span.quote: Therefore, in contrast with the celebrated role of weak ties in information access ( , 18 20 ), we find that both weak and strong ties have a relatively insignificant role as conduits for information (“the weakness of weak and strong ties” ): the former because the small amount of on-air time offers little chance of information transfer, and the latter because they are mostly confined within communities, with little access to new information.
